userStories.title: Allow a process-local environment overlay in gitWithTimeout
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Extend the shared git executor with an optional environment overlay so bot network git can receive credentials without changing the nax process environment.

**Motivation** — `nax bot fix` fetches and pushes with `git`, which has no way to receive a token from nax without writing it into `.git/config` or the command line.

**Approach** — `gitWithTimeout` (`packages/nax-agent/src/internal/git-exec.ts`)
- Baseline: `gitWithTimeout(args, workdir, timeoutMs?, maxBytes?, argvOverride?)`, spawn env `hardenedGitEnv(process.env)`.
- Target: `gitWithTimeout(args, workdir, timeoutMs?, maxBytes?, argvOverride?, envOverlay?: Readonly<Record<string, string>>)`, spawn env `hardenedGitEnv({ ...process.env, ...envOverlay })` when `envOverlay` is given, unchanged otherwise.

`gitWithTimeout` gains an optional sixth parameter `envOverlay`; when given, the spawned git process's environment is the hardened merge of `process.env` and the overlay. Callers that pass nothing are unchanged. Verification note: `bun run check:api` passes (the API snapshot lists names only).

Read-only integration: `gitSpawnEnv(overlay?)` (`packages/nax-agent/src/internal/git-env.ts`): `hardenedGitEnv({...process.env, ...overlay})`. Hardening adds `GIT_CONFIG_*` entries and leaves credential settings alone.

**Scope** — In: the shared executor's optional environment overlay and regression tests in its existing git-env suite. Out: identity capture and startup validation (US-002), gh/glab identity and authentication (US-003), and bot credential-helper selection and token overlay construction (US-004). Preserve the runtimeSpawn/_gitDeps seam, full argv override, hardened argv, timeout behavior, concurrent draining, and result shape; do not add Bun APIs to nax-agent.

**Interface** — Target call signature from the spec: `gitWithTimeout(args, workdir, timeoutMs?, maxBytes?, argvOverride?, envOverlay?: Readonly<Record<string, string>>)`. The first five arguments and existing Promise result stay unchanged; the sixth argument is optional and readonly.

Testing: write failing tests against _gitDeps.spawn with the shared makeSpawn helper before implementation; show them failing on old code. Assert the actual spawned environment, compare hardened GIT_CONFIG_* settings with the no-overlay path, and verify an overlay-bearing non-timeout git failure returns the existing stdout/stderr/exitCode result unchanged. Restore all seams and any ambient environment changes after each test.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] gitWithTimeout(["fetch"], "/repo", undefined, undefined, undefined, { NAX_FORGE_GIT_TOKEN: "tok-7f3a9c" }) spawns git with an environment whose NAX_FORGE_GIT_TOKEN is tok-7f3a9c.
[unit] gitWithTimeout called with an envOverlay still applies the hardened git settings: the spawned environment carries the same GIT_CONFIG_* entries as a call without an overlay.
[unit] gitWithTimeout(["status"], "/repo") with no overlay spawns git with an environment that has no NAX_FORGE_GIT_TOKEN key when process.env has none.

[unit] When gitWithTimeout(["fetch"], "/repo", undefined, undefined, undefined, { NAX_FORGE_GIT_TOKEN: "tok-7f3a9c" }) spawns git that exits 1 without timing out, with empty stdout and stderr authentication failed, it resolves to { stdout: "", stderr: "authentication failed", exitCode: 1 }, preserving the existing non-timeout failure result.

routing.reasoning: An additive trailing parameter in one shared executor is small, but it transports credentials into a child process and must preserve environment hardening; the security override requires strict three-session TDD.

suggestedCriteria: When process.env contains an environment key and gitWithTimeout receives a different value for that key in envOverlay, the spawned git environment contains the overlay value.
When gitWithTimeout receives envOverlay, process.env retains its original values after the call.

userStories.title: Capture and consume injected forge identity before CLI dispatch
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Capture a forge token from a deletable file into process-local state before constructing the CLI command tree, rejecting invalid input safely.

**Motivation** — A token in nax's environment reaches everything nax spawns.

**Approach** — The inputs:

| Variable | Required | Meaning |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `NAX_FORGE_TOKEN_FILE` | yes, to inject | Path to a file whose contents are the forge token. nax reads it once at CLI start and deletes it. |
| `NAX_FORGE_LOGIN` | GitHub: yes. GitLab: optional | The login the token acts as, in the REST form (`acme-bot[bot]` for a GitHub App). |
| `NAX_FORGE_USER_ID` | optional, needs a login | The numeric account id of that login. When present, identity comparisons use the id. |
| `NAX_FORGE_TOKEN` | never | Rejected: a token in the environment cannot be hidden from child processes. |

Rules, applied once at CLI start by `captureForgeIdentity(env)`; values are trimmed of surrounding whitespace first, and an empty value counts as absent. The token file is consumed first, so that no rejection leaves it on disk:

1. If `NAX_FORGE_TOKEN_FILE` is present, read it (`Bun.file(path).text()`, contents trimmed), then delete it (`_forgeIdentityDeps.deleteFile(path)`, by default `Bun.file(path).delete()`), whatever the rest of the input says. A delete that fails with `ENOENT` is not a failure (nothing is on disk). Any other delete failure: invalid, `NAX_FORGE_TOKEN_FILE could not be deleted`. nax never runs with the token still on disk. The guarantee covers the named path: when it is a symlink, the link is removed and the target is the caller's.
2. `NAX_FORGE_TOKEN` present: invalid, `NAX_FORGE_TOKEN is not supported; pass the token through NAX_FORGE_TOKEN_FILE`.
3. No token file, no login and no id: no identity; behaviour is exactly as before this feature.
4. A login or an id without a token file: invalid. The login is checked first: `NAX_FORGE_LOGIN requires NAX_FORGE_TOKEN_FILE`, else `NAX_FORGE_USER_ID requires NAX_FORGE_TOKEN_FILE`. It would change who nax trusts while the token in use stays the machine's ambient login.
5. An id without a login: invalid, `NAX_FORGE_USER_ID requires NAX_FORGE_LOGIN`.
6. `NAX_FORGE_USER_ID` must match `^[1-9][0-9]*$` and be at most `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`; otherwise invalid, `NAX_FORGE_USER_ID must be a positive integer`.
7. The read in rule 1 failed: invalid, `NAX_FORGE_TOKEN_FILE cannot be read`. The trimmed contents are empty: invalid, `NAX_FORGE_TOKEN_FILE is empty`.
8. Otherwise an identity `{ token, login?, id? }` is captured.

The rules are checked in that order; the first that fails decides the message. An invalid input makes the CLI write one line to stderr, `[forge] Invalid injected forge identity: <message>`, and exit 1 before any command runs. The `NaxError` carries code `FORGE_IDENTITY_INVALID` and context `{ stage: "forge" }`. No message or context contains the token value. `NAX_FORGE_LOGIN`, `NAX_FORGE_USER_ID` and `NAX_FORGE_TOKEN_FILE` stay in the environment; none is secret, and the file is gone. Logins are compared exactly as given (case-sensitive), as today.

The GitHub "login required" rule cannot be checked at startup (the forge is not known until a PR ref is resolved), so it is enforced in `readCurrentUser` (below).

`bin/nax.ts` imports `captureForgeIdentity` after the `agent-runtime/install` import and awaits `captureForgeIdentity(process.env)` before `new Command()`. ES imports are evaluated first, so the capture runs after module evaluation and before any command; no imported module spawns at import time. On `FORGE_IDENTITY_INVALID` it prints the message line to stderr and exits 1.

CLI entry: `packages/nax/bin/nax.ts`. Its first import must stay `../src/agent-runtime/install` (pinned by `test/unit/agent-runtime/install.test.ts`); it builds `const program = new Command()` and parses with `parseAsync`, which handles `--version`. Startup errors in `bin/` already use `console.error` + `process.exit(1)` (`bin/run-action.ts`).

**Scope** — In: the new identity module, its forge barrel exports, exact validation/error precedence and file consumption, and startup wiring before Commander construction. Out: reading identity in trust/defaultRun and GraphQL normalization (US-003), and bot network git credential transport (US-004). A token passed in the environment or on stdin; `NAX_FORGE_TOKEN` is rejected at startup. A token file on a read-only mount: the file must be deletable, or the CLI refuses to start. Hiding the identity from in-process plugin code that imports `@/forge`; the guarantee is about child processes and the token file. Propagating an injected identity to nax processes that nax itself launches (for example the jobs `nax chat` starts): they inherit `NAX_FORGE_TOKEN_FILE` naming a deleted file and refuse to start with `NAX_FORGE_TOKEN_FILE cannot be read`. Running `nax chat` with an injected identity is unsupported. A token containing an internal newline; the caller supplies a well-formed token. Minting, refreshing or rotating the token: the caller supplies a valid token per process; a process that outlives its token fails at the next forge call through the existing error path.

**Interface** — New, in `packages/nax/src/forge/identity.ts`, exported from the `@/forge` barrel:

```typescript
export interface InjectedForgeIdentity { readonly token: string; readonly login?: string; readonly id?: number }

export const FORGE_IDENTITY_ENV = {
  tokenFile: "NAX_FORGE_TOKEN_FILE",
  login: "NAX_FORGE_LOGIN",
  userId: "NAX_FORGE_USER_ID",
  rejectedToken: "NAX_FORGE_TOKEN",
} as const;

/** Mutable holder in the _deps style; tests set it and must reset it to undefined in afterEach. */
export const _forgeIdentity: { current: InjectedForgeIdentity | undefined } = { current: undefined };

/** Injectable file delete; the default is `(path) => Bun.file(path).delete()`. */
export const _forgeIdentityDeps: { deleteFile(path: string): Promise<void> };

/** Apply the input rules to `env`, read and delete the token file, store the result in
 *  `_forgeIdentity.current`. Resolves to the identity or undefined; rejects with NaxError code
 *  FORGE_IDENTITY_INVALID. */
export function captureForgeIdentity(env: Record<string, string | undefined>): Promise<InjectedForgeIdentity | undefined>;

export function injectedForgeIdentity(): InjectedForgeIdentity | undefined; // returns _forgeIdentity.current
```

Testing: The `[cli]` ACs spawn `bin/nax.ts`, as the existing `cli-trust-gate` and `cli-credentials-bootstrap` tests do: the entry-point wiring cannot be observed any other way. This is the documented exception to the `forbidden-patterns-tests.md` rule against spawning a full `nax` process: the two `[cli]` ACs stay the only ones that do. Tests that set `_forgeIdentity.current` reset it in `afterEach`, because suites run without isolation and a leaked identity changes other tests' `botGit` argv. Use tok-7f3a9c as the test token and real temporary token files for consumption tests. Restore _forgeIdentityDeps.deleteFile and environment state after each test. The startup failure contract is verified through the two specified CLI scenarios plus unit validation tests, not additional full-CLI cases.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] captureForgeIdentity({}) resolves to undefined and leaves _forgeIdentity.current undefined.

[unit] captureForgeIdentity({ NAX_FORGE_TOKEN_FILE: <file containing "tok-7f3a9c\n">, NAX_FORGE_LOGIN: "acme-bot[bot]" }) resolves to { token: "tok-7f3a9c", login: "acme-bot[bot]" }, and injectedForgeIdentity() then returns the same value.
[unit] With a token file and NAX_FORGE_LOGIN: "acme-bot[bot]", NAX_FORGE_USER_ID: "42", captureForgeIdentity resolves to an identity whose id is the number 42.
[unit] With only a token file, captureForgeIdentity resolves to { token: "tok-7f3a9c" } with no login and no id.
[unit] With a token file and NAX_FORGE_LOGIN: "  acme-bot[bot]\n", the resolved identity's login is acme-bot[bot].
[unit] After captureForgeIdentity resolves an identity from a token file, that file no longer exists.

[unit] captureForgeIdentity({ NAX_FORGE_TOKEN: "tok-7f3a9c" }) rejects with a NaxError code FORGE_IDENTITY_INVALID whose message contains NAX_FORGE_TOKEN is not supported, and the message text omits tok-7f3a9c.

[unit] captureForgeIdentity({ NAX_FORGE_TOKEN_FILE: "  ", NAX_FORGE_LOGIN: "acme-bot[bot]" }) rejects with a message containing NAX_FORGE_LOGIN requires NAX_FORGE_TOKEN_FILE (a blank path counts as absent).
[unit] With a token file and NAX_FORGE_USER_ID: "42" but no login, captureForgeIdentity rejects with a message containing NAX_FORGE_USER_ID requires NAX_FORGE_LOGIN.
[unit] With a token file, a login and NAX_FORGE_USER_ID: "4x", captureForgeIdentity rejects with a message containing NAX_FORGE_USER_ID must be a positive integer.
[unit] With a token file, a login and NAX_FORGE_USER_ID: "9007199254740993", captureForgeIdentity rejects with a message containing NAX_FORGE_USER_ID must be a positive integer.
[unit] With NAX_FORGE_TOKEN_FILE naming a path that does not exist, captureForgeIdentity rejects with a message containing NAX_FORGE_TOKEN_FILE cannot be read.
[unit] With a token file whose contents are only whitespace, captureForgeIdentity rejects with a message containing NAX_FORGE_TOKEN_FILE is empty.

[unit] With a token file and _forgeIdentityDeps.deleteFile stubbed to throw an EACCES error, captureForgeIdentity rejects with a message containing NAX_FORGE_TOKEN_FILE could not be deleted, and the message text omits tok-7f3a9c.
[unit] With NAX_FORGE_TOKEN: "tok-7f3a9c" and a valid token file, captureForgeIdentity rejects with a message containing NAX_FORGE_TOKEN is not supported, and the token file no longer exists.
[unit] With a valid token file, a login and NAX_FORGE_USER_ID: "4x", after captureForgeIdentity rejects, the token file no longer exists.
[unit] With no token file, NAX_FORGE_LOGIN: "acme-bot[bot]" and NAX_FORGE_USER_ID: "42", captureForgeIdentity rejects with a message containing NAX_FORGE_LOGIN requires NAX_FORGE_TOKEN_FILE.
[unit] captureForgeIdentity({ NAX_FORGE_USER_ID: "42" }) rejects with a message containing NAX_FORGE_USER_ID requires NAX_FORGE_TOKEN_FILE.
[unit] With a token file, a login and NAX_FORGE_USER_ID: "042", captureForgeIdentity rejects with a message containing NAX_FORGE_USER_ID must be a positive integer.
[unit] With a token file, a login and NAX_FORGE_USER_ID: "9007199254740991", the resolved identity's id is 9007199254740991.
[cli] Running bin/nax.ts --version with NAX_FORGE_LOGIN=acme-bot[bot] and no NAX_FORGE_TOKEN_FILE exits 1 and writes a stderr line beginning [forge] Invalid injected forge identity:.

[cli] Running bin/nax.ts --version with NAX_FORGE_TOKEN_FILE naming a file containing tok-7f3a9c and NAX_FORGE_LOGIN=acme-bot[bot] exits 0, prints the version, and the token file no longer exists afterwards.
When captureForgeIdentity rejects an invalid input, the rejection is a NaxError with code FORGE_IDENTITY_INVALID and context { stage: "forge" }, without the token value in its message or context.

routing.reasoning: One new identity module plus an existing barrel and CLI startup hook use established Bun filesystem, NaxError, and mutable-deps patterns; ordered token consumption is bounded medium work, while credential secrecy requires the three-session security override.

suggestedCriteria: When _forgeIdentityDeps.deleteFile throws ENOENT after a successful token read, captureForgeIdentity resolves to the captured identity.
When NAX_FORGE_TOKEN_FILE names a symlink to a readable token file, captureForgeIdentity removes the symlink and leaves its target file present.
When the token file read fails and NAX_FORGE_TOKEN is also present, captureForgeIdentity rejects with NAX_FORGE_TOKEN is not supported; pass the token through NAX_FORGE_TOKEN_FILE.
When deletion fails with EACCES and NAX_FORGE_TOKEN is also present, captureForgeIdentity rejects with NAX_FORGE_TOKEN_FILE could not be deleted.
When all four identity inputs contain only whitespace, captureForgeIdentity resolves to undefined.
When captureForgeIdentity consumes a valid token file, the supplied env object's NAX_FORGE_LOGIN, NAX_FORGE_USER_ID, and NAX_FORGE_TOKEN_FILE values remain unchanged.

userStories.title: Use injected identity consistently for forge trust and subprocesses
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Route forge identity checks and gh/glab authentication through the captured identity while preserving ambient behavior when none is supplied.

**Motivation** — A GitHub App installation token cannot call `/user`, so `readCurrentUser` fails.

**Approach** — `readCurrentUser(ref, deps, cwd)`:
- identity with a login: returns `{ login, id? }` from the identity and makes no `deps.run` call;
- identity without a login on GitHub: throws `NaxError` code `FORGE_IDENTITY_LOGIN_REQUIRED` with message `[forge] NAX_FORGE_LOGIN is required with NAX_FORGE_TOKEN_FILE on GitHub`; `classifyPrTrust` already turns a thrown `readCurrentUser` into an untrusted result (fail closed);
- identity without a login on GitLab: calls `api user` as today; the token reaches `glab` through `defaultRun`, so the answer is the token's own bot user;
- no identity: unchanged.

GitHub review-thread authors: the GraphQL query in `forge/threads.ts` (`REVIEW_THREADS_QUERY`) also asks for the author's `__typename`; `githubThread` maps an author whose `__typename` is `Bot` to `<login>[bot]`, the REST form. GitHub's GraphQL API returns a bot's login without the `[bot]` suffix, so without this a bot's own thread comments never match its REST-form login, and a human account named like the bot's slug could pass as the bot. A `User` author keeps its login unchanged.

`defaultRun(cmd, opts)`: when an identity is captured and the program `cmd[0]` is `gh` (the bare name or a path ending in `/gh`), the spawn environment gains `GH_TOKEN=<token>` and `GH_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN=<token>` (`gh` reads the second for GitHub Enterprise Server hosts); when it is `glab` (bare or a path ending in `/glab`), it gains `GITLAB_TOKEN=<token>`. Any other program (including `git`) gets no token. The token is never added to `cmd`.

Because every forge-touching command reads identity through `readCurrentUser` and spawns through `defaultRun`, the identity applies to `nax bot review`, `nax bot fix`, the workflow commands that post threads or rulings, and the finish phase's forge calls, with no per-command wiring. This is deliberate: a half-switched identity (bot posts as the injected login, a workflow command still compares against the ambient login) would break own-comment discovery.

Read-only integration:
- `classifyPrTrust(ref: PrRef, info: PrInfo, deps: ForgeDeps, cwd: string): Promise<PrTrust>` (`packages/nax/src/forge/trust.ts`): compares `info.author` with `readCurrentUser`, by id when both ids are present, else by login; falls back to `hasWriteAccess` (`forge/access.ts`). The PR author comes from REST (`forge/pr-read.ts`, `reply.user.login`), so it is already in the `[bot]` form.
- `findOwnComments(ref, deps, cwd)` (`forge/marker.ts`): `readCurrentUser` then `ownComments(comments, user.login)`, an exact string comparison.

Changed integration:
- `ForgeDeps` (`packages/nax/src/forge/types.ts`)
  - Baseline: `{ run(cmd, opts); readText(path) }`.
  - Target: adds optional `identity?(): InjectedForgeIdentity | undefined`. `defaultForgeDeps.identity` returns the captured identity. Test fakes that omit it behave as "no identity".
- `readCurrentUser` (`forge/trust.ts`): same signature; reads `deps.identity?.()` first (rules above).
- `REVIEW_THREADS_QUERY` / `githubThread` (`forge/threads.ts`)
  - Baseline: `author { login }`; `author: comment.author?.login ?? "ghost"`.
  - Target: `author { login __typename }`; a `Bot` author maps to `<login>[bot]`, anything else as before.
- `defaultRun` (`forge/deps.ts`): same signature; spawn env becomes `gitSpawnEnv(overlay)` with the token overlay above, `gitSpawnEnv()` when no identity or another program.

Failure handling: GitHub PR, token injected, no login: `readCurrentUser` throws `FORGE_IDENTITY_LOGIN_REQUIRED`; `classifyPrTrust` returns untrusted with a reason naming the failure; no `api user` call. Forge rejects the injected token (expired, missing permission): Unchanged existing behaviour: the `gh` / `glab` / `git` call fails and its existing error path reports it. No retry and no fallback to the ambient login (see Out of Scope).

**Scope** — In: optional ForgeDeps identity accessor, injected current-user resolution, Bot GraphQL author normalization, defaultForgeDeps wiring, gh/glab-only token env overlays, and the trust/ownership/transport seam tests. Out: capture/startup implementation (US-002) and bot network git credentials (US-004); do not reimplement either. The auto-pr builtin plugin's own subprocess runner (`plugins/builtin/auto-pr/index.ts`) and the finish phase's own `git push` (`finish/commit.ts`): they do not receive the token from this feature. GitLab thread and note author forms: GitLab returns the same `username` from every API, so no mapping is added. Case-insensitive login matching; `NAX_FORGE_LOGIN` must match the forge's login exactly, or own-comment and trust checks fail closed. Migrating comments or threads posted under a previous login; after a switch they no longer count as the bot's own. Self-managed GitLab host selection (`GITLAB_HOST`); `GITLAB_TOKEN` is applied to whatever host `glab` resolves. Live verification against a real GitLab project or group access token; GitLab is covered by unit tests with fakes only. Handling a forge that rejects the injected token: no new retry, no fallback to the ambient login, and no new error message; the existing per-call error paths are unchanged.

**Interface** — Preserve `readCurrentUser(ref: PrRef, deps: ForgeDeps, cwd: string): Promise<CurrentUser>` and `defaultRun(cmd, opts)` signatures. Add the optional contract member exactly: `identity?(): InjectedForgeIdentity | undefined`. `defaultForgeDeps.identity` returns the captured identity through `injectedForgeIdentity()` from US-002.

Testing: create identity-trust.test.ts for injected readCurrentUser, existing classifyPrTrust rules, GraphQL Bot/User distinction, and findOwnComments through the real readers with fake API replies. Create deps-identity.test.ts for defaultForgeDeps and executable temporary gh/glab/other fixtures. A fixture prints requested values with `printf '%s'` (no trailing newline); use token tok-7f3a9c. The `defaultRun` fixture ACs set identity through `captureForgeIdentity` and observe subprocess stdout, proving capture-to-transport wiring. Fixture calls pass the required second argument `{ cwd: <tmp> }`; the temporary directory placeholder is resolved to the fixture directory. For rejected-token fixtures, count invocations and assert the unchanged non-timeout exitCode/stdout/stderr result so the no-retry/no-fallback contract is observable. Restore _forgeIdentity.current to undefined in afterEach and restore environment state. Keep no-identity fake compatibility, query fixture compatibility without __typename, exact argv, hardened git env, timeout/result behavior, and process cleanup unchanged.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] readCurrentUser for a GitHub ref, with deps.identity() returning { token: "tok-7f3a9c", login: "acme-bot[bot]" }, returns { login: "acme-bot[bot]" } and never calls deps.run.
[unit] readCurrentUser with deps.identity() returning { token: "tok-7f3a9c", login: "acme-bot[bot]", id: 42 } returns { login: "acme-bot[bot]", id: 42 }.
[unit] readCurrentUser for a GitHub ref with deps.identity() returning { token: "tok-7f3a9c" } throws a NaxError with code FORGE_IDENTITY_LOGIN_REQUIRED and never calls deps.run.

[unit] readCurrentUser(ref, deps, "/repo") for a GitLab ref with deps.identity() returning { token: "tok-7f3a9c" } calls deps.run once with ["glab", "api", "--hostname", ref.host, "user"] and { cwd: "/repo" }, and returns a CurrentUser whose login is the username from that reply.
[unit] readCurrentUser with a deps that has no identity member calls deps.run with the api user argv, as before this feature.
[unit] classifyPrTrust for a same-repo PR authored by acme-bot[bot], with an injected login acme-bot[bot], returns trusted: true with reason author is the current user.

[unit] classifyPrTrust for a same-repo PR authored by alice (write access granted by the fake's permission reply), with an injected login acme-bot[bot], returns trusted: true with reason author has write access.
[unit] classifyPrTrust for a GitHub PR with deps.identity() returning { token: "tok-7f3a9c" } returns trusted: false with a reason that contains NAX_FORGE_LOGIN is required.
[unit] listReviewThreads on GitHub sends a query= argument in which the comment author selection includes __typename.
[unit] listReviewThreads on GitHub, given a GraphQL reply whose thread comment author is { login: "acme-bot", __typename: "Bot" }, returns that comment with author acme-bot[bot].
[unit] listReviewThreads on GitHub, given a thread comment author { login: "acme-bot", __typename: "User" }, returns that comment with author acme-bot.

[unit] findOwnComments on GitHub with an injected login acme-bot[bot] returns a marked thread comment whose GraphQL author is { login: "acme-bot", __typename: "Bot" }, and does not return a marked thread comment whose author is { login: "acme-bot", __typename: "User" }.
[unit] defaultForgeDeps.identity() returns the value set in _forgeIdentity.current.
[unit] After captureForgeIdentity captures { token: "tok-7f3a9c", login: "acme-bot[bot]" }, defaultRun([<tmp>/gh], { cwd: <tmp> }), a fixture that prints $GH_TOKEN, returns stdout tok-7f3a9c.
[unit] With that identity captured, defaultRun([<tmp>/gh], { cwd: <tmp> }), a fixture that prints $GH_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN, returns stdout tok-7f3a9c.
[unit] With that identity captured, defaultRun([<tmp>/glab], { cwd: <tmp> }), a fixture that prints $GITLAB_TOKEN, returns stdout tok-7f3a9c.
[unit] With that identity captured, defaultRun([<tmp>/other], { cwd: <tmp> }), a fixture that prints $GH_TOKEN$GITLAB_TOKEN, returns stdout that is not tok-7f3a9c and does not include it.
[unit] With that identity captured, defaultRun([<tmp>/gh, "api", "user"], { cwd: <tmp> }), a fixture that prints its arguments joined by a space, returns stdout api user.
[unit] With no identity captured and GH_TOKEN absent from process.env, defaultRun([<tmp>/gh], { cwd: <tmp> }) with the $GH_TOKEN fixture returns empty stdout.

When a gh or glab fixture rejects the injected token before the timeout with exitCode 1, empty stdout and stderr authentication failed, defaultRun returns { exitCode: 1, stdout: "", stderr: "authentication failed" } after exactly one fixture invocation, preserving the existing failure output without retrying or falling back to the ambient login.

routing.reasoning: Four existing forge modules gain an optional accessor, early identity branches, a Bot author mapping, and spawn-local env selection without new architecture or caller rewiring; authentication and trust changes still mandate the three-session security override.

suggestedCriteria: When defaultRun runs git with a captured identity and no corresponding ambient token variables, the git subprocess environment contains none of the injected GH_TOKEN, GH_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN, GITLAB_TOKEN, or NAX_FORGE_GIT_TOKEN values.
When defaultRun runs a program whose name is gh-wrapper or notgh with a captured identity, the program's environment does not contain the injected token.
When defaultRun invokes the bare names gh and glab resolved through PATH with a captured identity, gh receives both GH_TOKEN and GH_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN and glab receives GITLAB_TOKEN.
When listReviewThreads receives a GitHub author without __typename, the returned author's login remains unchanged as in existing fixtures.
When classifyPrTrust receives matching author and injected-user ids with different logins on a same-repo PR, it returns trusted: true with reason author is the current user.
When classifyPrTrust receives differing author and injected-user ids but matching logins, it does not trust the PR on the basis of author is the current user.
When readCurrentUser receives a GitHub ref and an injected token without login, its error message is [forge] NAX_FORGE_LOGIN is required with NAX_FORGE_TOKEN_FILE on GitHub.

userStories.title: Authenticate bot fetch and push with an ephemeral credential helper
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Authenticate only botGit fetch/push subprocesses with the captured token through a process-local environment overlay and a non-persisting HTTPS credential helper.

**Motivation** — `nax bot fix` fetches and pushes with `git`, which has no way to receive a token from nax without writing it into `.git/config` or the command line.

**Approach** — `botGit(args, ...)` (`packages/nax/src/bot/git.ts`): when an identity is captured and the git verb (`args[0]`; every current caller passes the verb first) is `fetch` or `push`, the argv gains `-c credential.helper=` (clears every configured helper) followed by `-c credential.helper=<NAX_BOT_CREDENTIAL_HELPER>`, and that one process gets `NAX_FORGE_GIT_TOKEN=<token>` and `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` (a rejected token fails instead of prompting) through the new `gitWithTimeout` env overlay. The helper answers a `get` whose input carries `protocol=https` with `username=x-access-token` and `password=$NAX_FORGE_GIT_TOKEN`; for any other protocol, and for `store` / `erase`, it prints nothing. `x-access-token` is the GitHub App HTTPS username, and GitLab accepts any non-empty username with a token. Other verbs are unchanged. The token is never written to `.git/config` and never appears in argv.

New, in `packages/nax/src/bot/git.ts`: `NAX_BOT_CREDENTIAL_HELPER`, the helper string in git's shell function form, `!f() { ...; }; f`. Git strips the leading `!`, appends the action, and runs the rest with `sh -c`, so `$1` is the action and the `protocol=` / `host=` lines arrive on stdin. It prints with `printf '%s\n'` and exits 0 in every case. The ACs drive it through that same harness: the string without its leading `!`, followed by the action, run by `sh -c` with the input on stdin.

Changed integration: `botGit` (`bot/git.ts`): same signature; adds the credential-helper prefix and env overlay above.

Read-only integration:
- `gitSpawnEnv(overlay?)` (`packages/nax-agent/src/internal/git-env.ts`): `hardenedGitEnv({...process.env, ...overlay})`. Hardening adds `GIT_CONFIG_*` entries and leaves credential settings alone.
- Network bot git call sites, all through `botGit`: `fetch` in `bot/checkout.ts`, `push --dry-run` in `checkPushAccess` (`bot/fix-input.ts`), `push` in `pushStep` (`bot/fix-steps.ts`).

The commit author of a `nax bot fix` commit is not decided by nax: the caller sets the standard `GIT_AUTHOR_NAME` / `GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL` / `GIT_COMMITTER_NAME` / `GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL` variables if it wants bot-authored commits, and nax passes them through as it does today.

Failure handling: Forge rejects the injected token (expired, missing permission): Unchanged existing behaviour: the `gh` / `glab` / `git` call fails and its existing error path reports it. No retry and no fallback to the ambient login (see Out of Scope).

**Scope** — In: botGit's fetch/push credential prefix, exported NAX_BOT_CREDENTIAL_HELPER string, sixth-argument environment overlay from US-001, unchanged hooks-off ordering, and end-to-end helper and checkPushAccess seam tests. Out: identity capture/startup (US-002), forge identity resolution and gh/glab transport (US-003), and changing the shared git executor (US-001). Scoping the git credential helper to one host: it answers any `https` host `origin` points at, which is the repository the caller pointed nax at. Setting the commit author of `nax bot fix` commits; the caller uses the standard `GIT_AUTHOR_*` / `GIT_COMMITTER_*` variables. The auto-pr builtin plugin's own subprocess runner (`plugins/builtin/auto-pr/index.ts`) and the finish phase's own `git push` (`finish/commit.ts`): they do not receive the token from this feature. `botGit` verb detection behind a leading global git option (`-C`, `-c`); every current caller passes the verb as `args[0]`. Handling a forge that rejects the injected token: no new retry, no fallback to the ambient login, and no new error message; the existing per-call error paths are unchanged.

**Interface** — Preserve the existing botGit signature and return type:
```typescript
export function botGit(
  args: string[],
  workdir: string,
  timeoutMs?: number,
  maxBytes?: number,
): ReturnType<typeof gitWithTimeout>
```
The new constant is `NAX_BOT_CREDENTIAL_HELPER`; its value is a shell function-form helper, `!f() { ...; }; f`, not a string containing the token. Read the captured identity through `injectedForgeIdentity()` from US-002. Consume US-001's optional sixth parameter `envOverlay?: Readonly<Record<string, string>>` while retaining argvOverride as the fifth parameter. For authenticated fetch/push the argv order is git, -c, core.hooksPath=/dev/null, -c, credential.helper=, -c, credential.helper=<NAX_BOT_CREDENTIAL_HELPER>, then the original verb and arguments.

Testing: create unit/bot/git-identity.test.ts using _gitDeps.spawn and the existing makeSpawn helper. The `botGit` / `checkPushAccess` ACs set the identity through `captureForgeIdentity` and observe the spawn; leave _fixInputDeps.runGit at its default for the checkPushAccess case. Assert the actual spawned NAX_FORGE_GIT_TOKEN and GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT environment values, not only a mocked gitWithTimeout argument. Create integration/bot/credential-helper.test.ts using a real git credential fill in a temporary repository, including a conflicting local credential.helper, plus the exact sh -c helper harness for get/store/erase and non-HTTPS. Do not contact a real forge. Use tok-7f3a9c and restore _forgeIdentity.current to undefined, spawn seams, environment state, and temporary files in afterEach. Existing bot/git.test.ts no-identity argv and hardening anchors must remain unchanged.

analysis:
This is a security-sensitive enhancement to existing forge and bot infrastructure, not greenfield work. Navigation used direct reads and text search because codebase-memory MCP tools were unavailable. All paths below are repository-root relative. The binding decomposition is exactly US-001 through US-004: US-001 in packages/nax-agent and US-002 in packages/nax can start independently; US-003 follows US-002; US-004 follows US-001 and US-002. All four stories manipulate token or credential transport and therefore require three-session-tdd, even where the code change is small.

Architecture and conventions: docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md:11 links the focused architecture rules, and docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md:164 summarizes dependency injection, function limits, error prefixes, and testing conventions. nax uses Bun-native filesystem and spawn APIs; nax-agent must remain Node-compatible and spawn through the runtime slot. No new packages or external dependencies are needed. nax-agent's internal entry already re-exports git-env and git-exec (packages/nax-agent/src/internal.ts:38 and packages/nax-agent/src/internal.ts:39). nax's utils/git re-exports the same gitWithTimeout and _gitDeps objects (packages/nax/src/utils/git.ts:15); change the shared implementation, not a nax-only duplicate. Import shared nax functionality through its public barrels where required. packages/nax/src/forge/index.ts:1 documents the forge barrel boundary. NaxError is re-exported by packages/nax/src/errors.ts:7; its canonical constructor accepts arbitrary string codes and a context object (packages/nax-agent/src/infra/nax-error.ts:6), so no new error-code registry is necessary.

Its environment currently comes from hardenedGitEnv(process.env) at packages/nax-agent/src/internal/git-exec.ts:86. Append envOverlay as an optional sixth parameter without changing the first five, timeout behavior, bounded concurrent stream draining, kill behavior, result shape, or argv hardening. packages/nax-agent/src/internal/git-env.ts:52 appends core.fsmonitor=false, diff.ignoreSubmodules=dirty, and submodule.recurse=false via GIT_CONFIG_*; packages/nax-agent/src/internal/git-env.ts:71 already demonstrates merge-before-hardening in gitSpawnEnv. The overlay must override matching process.env keys but must not be spread over an already-hardened result. Preserve the no-overlay path exactly. Existing coverage in packages/nax-agent/test/unit/internal/git-env.test.ts:100 exercises gitSpawnEnv, :125 exercises real fsmonitor protection, and :144 exercises argvOverride through makeSpawn and withDepsRestore. Extend that existing test file for the three overlay ACs; US-001 needs no new file. bun run check:api is a verification step, not an AC; the API snapshot records names only, and this story adds no export name.

US-002 baseline and impact: packages/nax/bin/nax.ts:36 must remain the first import, importing ../src/agent-runtime/install; packages/nax/test/unit/agent-runtime/install.test.ts:11 pins it. The command tree currently starts at packages/nax/bin/nax.ts:129 with new Command(). Capture must be awaited before this statement, not merely before parseAsync; --version is handled by Commander and must not bypass validation or file consumption. configureNaxCredentials and parseAsync currently occur at packages/nax/bin/nax.ts:1746 and :1748. Existing bottom-of-file error formatting prepends Error:, so startup identity errors need their own exact one-line [forge] handling rather than flowing through that wrapper. Consume the token file before any other input rejection: attempt read once and delete the named path even if reading fails or another input is invalid. Delete ENOENT is success; other deletion errors outrank all subsequent validation errors. Delay reporting a read failure until after the earlier validation rules. Trim every input; blank means absent; validate id by canonical positive-decimal syntax and safe-integer range. Capture a successful identity only after validation, and never include token text in message, context, or diagnostics. Named symlink deletion removes the link, not its target; do not add realpath-following deletion. NAX_FORGE_LOGIN, NAX_FORGE_USER_ID, and NAX_FORGE_TOKEN_FILE stay in the environment. The safe boundary is never placing the supplied secret in the parent environment. Existing CLI process-test patterns are packages/nax/test/integration/cli/cli-trust-gate.test.ts:57 and packages/nax/test/integration/cli/cli-credentials-bootstrap.test.ts:13, using an explicit env and concurrent output reads. US-004 baseline and impact: packages/nax/src/bot/git.ts:6 is a thin botGit wrapper; :4 fixes BOT_GIT_HOOKS_OFF, and :13 passes a full argvOverride to gitWithTimeout. Keep hook suppression first, then for args[0] fetch/push only add -c credential.helper= and -c credential.helper=<NAX_BOT_CREDENTIAL_HELPER>. Supply NAX_FORGE_GIT_TOKEN and GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 via the sixth parameter from US-001, not global environment mutation. Local verbs and no-identity calls retain existing argv/environment. The helper must work under POSIX sh, answer only get plus protocol=https, consume protocol/host lines from stdin, emit username=x-access-token and password from the process-local token using printf '%s\n', emit nothing for other protocols/store/erase, and always exit 0. Integration tests need real git credential fill in a temporary local repository and the exact sh -c harness git uses, not network access. Verify clearing a repository-local credential.helper that otherwise supplies password=wrong.

Compatibility and migration: changes are opt-in and additive. No configuration schema, manifests, package versions, public command flags, or user data need migration. The spec's 'Modifies None' paragraph denotes no breaking signatures/fixture migration; implementation necessarily edits existing files named in the Integration section. gitWithTimeout adds an optional trailing argument and ForgeDeps adds an optional member, so existing callers/fakes remain valid. With no captured identity every spawn argv/environment remains unchanged. Older GraphQL fixtures lacking __typename retain their login. With an identity, authentication failures retain existing nonzero/error reporting, with no retries or fallback to ambient credentials. GitHub token-only input is accepted at startup and rejected only once a GitHub ref reaches readCurrentUser; GitLab token-only input uses authenticated glab api user. The caller must supply a fresh deletable token file per process, exact REST-form login, and optional standard GIT_AUTHOR_*/GIT_COMMITTER_* environment values for commit authorship. Nested nax launches and nax chat with this identity are unsupported.

Verification and risk controls: prove regression tests fail against the old implementation before changes, then run targeted bun:test paths within the owning package; never bare bun test or bun run nax. All new identity-setting tests reset _forgeIdentity.current in afterEach to avoid changing unrelated botGit assertions. Restore _forgeIdentityDeps.deleteFile, _gitDeps.spawn, and any environment/test fixture state. Preserve process-level timeouts and cleanup in real-spawn tests. Failure-table requirements are represented in the owning story, including startup rejection, missing GitHub login fail-closed trust, and rejected-token no-retry/no-fallback paths through existing forge/git errors. Quality gates remain verification steps rather than behavioral ACs. No coverage command should run inside a NAX_SANDBOXED=1 session. Primary risks are validation-precedence drift leaving token files behind, leaking secrets through parent env/argv/error context, import-order regressions, inconsistent identity across forge consumers, GraphQL Bot versus User ambiguity, credential-helper ordering/quoting, and shared-state pollution. The architecture deliberately limits token delivery to nax's own gh/glab spawns and botGit fetch/push; it does not claim protection from in-process plugins or unrelated preexisting ambient credentials.

Refine audit: enumerated and matched all 58 spec ACs in their original stories: US-001 3/3, US-002 22/22, US-003 19/19, US-004 14/14. Preserved regression qualifiers including same hardened entries as no overlay, blank path counts as absent, as before this feature, the fake permission reply, GH_TOKEN absent from process.env, _fixInputDeps.runGit left at its default, and the parenthetical explaining that the empty helper entry clears configured helpers. All 17 top-level exclusions are preserved verbatim. The three failure-table rows map to US-002 startup errors, US-003 missing GitHub login, and US-003/US-004 unchanged token-rejection paths. Added an explicit non-timeout git-failure regression AC to US-001, which previously had only a no-token negative condition rather than a failed-operation case. All four stories now have directly observable negative paths and backward-compatibility anchors. Corrected the fixture AC shorthand to supply defaultRun's required opts argument (packages/nax/src/forge/deps.ts:39), clarified GitLab reply.username maps to CurrentUser.login through the explicit host-aware argv (packages/nax/src/forge/trust.ts:14 and :25), and made GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT's string representation explicit. The required current-source context lists now match all five spec recommendations for US-002 and US-003, replacing lower-priority entries rather than exceeding five. Binding story ids, workdirs, dependencies, and produced files are unchanged. Reclassified US-002 through US-004 as medium because the changes extend bounded existing patterns with no framework or architectural redesign; all retain three-session-tdd under the mandatory security override. US-001 remains simple with the same override. No description contradicts its ACs or assigns another story's implementation work to itself; boundary-adjacent exclusions are echoed in the relevant Scope sections.
outOfScope: Minting, refreshing or rotating the token: the caller supplies a valid token per process; a process that outlives its token fails at the next forge call through the existing error path.
Handling a forge that rejects the injected token: no new retry, no fallback to the ambient login, and no new error message; the existing per-call error paths are unchanged.
A token passed in the environment or on stdin; `NAX_FORGE_TOKEN` is rejected at startup.
A token file on a read-only mount: the file must be deletable, or the CLI refuses to start.
Live verification against a real GitLab project or group access token; GitLab is covered by unit tests with fakes only.
Self-managed GitLab host selection (`GITLAB_HOST`); `GITLAB_TOKEN` is applied to whatever host `glab` resolves.
Scoping the git credential helper to one host: it answers any `https` host `origin` points at, which is the repository the caller pointed nax at.
Setting the commit author of `nax bot fix` commits; the caller uses the standard `GIT_AUTHOR_*` / `GIT_COMMITTER_*` variables.
The auto-pr builtin plugin's own subprocess runner (`plugins/builtin/auto-pr/index.ts`) and the finish phase's own `git push` (`finish/commit.ts`): they do not receive the token from this feature.
GitLab thread and note author forms: GitLab returns the same `username` from every API, so no mapping is added.
Migrating comments or threads posted under a previous login; after a switch they no longer count as the bot's own.
Hiding the identity from in-process plugin code that imports `@/forge`; the guarantee is about child processes and the token file.

Propagating an injected identity to nax processes that nax itself launches (for example the jobs `nax chat` starts): they inherit `NAX_FORGE_TOKEN_FILE` naming a deleted file and refuse to start with `NAX_FORGE_TOKEN_FILE cannot be read`. Running `nax chat` with an injected identity is unsupported.
Case-insensitive login matching; `NAX_FORGE_LOGIN` must match the forge's login exactly, or own-comment and trust checks fail closed.
A token containing an internal newline; the caller supplies a well-formed token.
`botGit` verb detection behind a leading global git option (`-C`, `-c`); every current caller passes the verb as `args[0]`.
